newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B share index ends down on correction.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B share index ends down on correction.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended down on Thursday on a correction in line with the city's domestic A share market following sharp gains in the past few days, but market sentiment remained good, brokers said.
The B index fell 0.675 points or 0.94 percent to 70.944 points on volume of 40.1 million shares worth $18.1 million, up from Wednesday's $15.6 million.
The A share index edged down 9.237 points or 0.78 percent to 1,168.466 points on volume of 839.1 million shares worth 8.8 billion yuan, down from 9.7 billion yuan on Wednesday.
"Domestic investors began profit-taking after the consecutive rises of the past few days," one broker said. "But trading remained active on bargain-hunting."
"The index will find support at around 68-69 points if there are no major negative factors," a second broker said.
All 43 B shares traded, with 28 down, one flat and 14 up.

Textile machinery maker Shanghai Erfangji Co was the biggest loser on expectations of poor 1996 results despite active domestic speculative buying, slipping $0.014 or 7.21 percent to $0.18 on volume of 1.8 million shares.
Real estate developer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development traded the most on institutional buying, ending down $0.002 or 0.21 percent to $0.932 on volume of three million shares.
Shanghai's A share index ended down on profit-taking after sharp gains over the past few days, brokers said.
The SSE 30 blue-chip index slipped 21.015 points or 0.7 percent to 3002.632 points.
Shanghai Bus Industrial Co was the biggest loser on its plan not to make a bonus issue, falling 0.74 yuan or 5.87 percent to 14.85 yuan on volume of 4.2 million shares.
